object_description: rotated, lowered sports-hall volume with shed roofs
design_condition: The hall is rotated to align with surrounding residential and school buildings, lowered to limit its height, and positioned to preserve a clear forecourt while concentrating remaining outdoor uses along the plot boundaries.

positive.statement: The rotation creates an interesting forecourt where the main entrance is clearly visible.

position.rationale: The rotated footprint forms an identifiable open approach zone along the lower-right forecourt edge.

positive.statement: The building is cleverly placed and hardly causes any disruption to the neighborhood despite its size.

position.rationale: Neighborhood disruption and placement are evaluated at overall site scale.

positive.statement: The clear site-planning concept and appropriate architectural design are convincing in some areas.

position.rationale: The rotated large footprint and boundary-oriented outdoor zones are legible across plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The functionally designed double sports hall has a calm interior atmosphere with sufficient natural lighting.

position.rationale: The central hall zone is approximated within the large sampled volume; interior atmosphere is not directly visible.

positive.statement: The planned spatial structure allows the desired flexibility in the arrangement of studios and classrooms.

position.rationale: Flexible learning spaces are approximated along the side zones of the broad building footprint.

positive.statement: The proportion of glass can be precisely adapted to orientation, use and individual daylight needs.

position.rationale: Facade glazing is assigned to the exposed eastern envelope, though glass itself is not separately identifiable.

positive.statement: The requirements for ecology and sustainability are adequately depicted and described.

position.rationale: The judgment concerns documented environmental performance rather than a physical model location.

positive.statement: The fire-protection, escape-route and building-physics requirements are planned in a comprehensible manner.

position.rationale: Code compliance and escape planning are not spatially identifiable in the exterior point cloud.

negative.statement: The very large footprint comes at the expense of the surrounding areas.

position.rationale: The extensive low building footprint dominates the plan and is corroborated by all elevations.

negative.statement: The many parking spaces occupy almost the entire central outdoor area.

position.rationale: Parking is approximated in the central forecourt zone, without individually visible parking elements.

negative.statement: The entrances are sometimes narrow and winding.

position.rationale: Entrance access is constrained to the rotated forecourt edge where the approach meets the building.

negative.statement: There are no shady trees, so the large surface area would heat up significantly in summer.

position.rationale: Potential tree planting is assigned to the boundary landscape zone; vegetation is not distinctly sampled.

negative.statement: The proportion of green space is very low, which is negative ecologically and for the microclimate.

position.rationale: Green-space deficiency concerns the distributed perimeter and residual outdoor areas.

negative.statement: The lighting of the rooms in the inner layer is judged to be insufficient.

position.rationale: The inner layer is approximated near the central mass, though rooms are not separately visible.

negative.statement: Separate narrow stairs serve both uses regardless of opening times.

position.rationale: Stair access is approximated along a side circulation zone without distinct stair geometry.

negative.statement: The point skylights lead to uneven lighting and are disadvantageous for sports activities.

position.rationale: Roof-level punctuated features are visible across the sampled shed-roof surfaces.

negative.statement: The roof construction is judged to be complex and its statics are unresolved at the roof valleys.

position.rationale: Valley concerns are assigned to the upper roof junctions visible in the stepped elevations.

negative.statement: The wooden slats are unsuitable because of shadows in the sports hall and concerns about cleaning.

position.rationale: Slatted screening is approximated on the exposed facade; shadows and cleaning are not geometrically represented.

negative.statement: A clear design concept for the outdoor spaces and user-friendly environmental planning is missing.

position.rationale: The criticism addresses the overall site concept rather than one identifiable outdoor feature.

negative.statement: There is no coherent parking solution because the dual use of central zones is realistic only when parking spaces are closed.

position.rationale: Dual-use parking is assigned to the central outdoor zone, where its arrangement is not explicitly distinguishable.
